s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent lesion of the nasal vestibule with local invasion
salient_findings: Recurrent lesion of the right nasal vestibule mucosa
Tumor within the nasal vestibule floor and ala
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
Never-smoker
Initial lesion biopsied 5 years prior
Initial biopsy reported as solid and cystic hidradenoma
p63 positive, pancytokeratin positive, and p16 negative on initial biopsy
Lesion recurred 8 months prior to presentation
Second excision showed p63 positive and p16 negative with positive margins
Enlarged, firm right ala on examination
Tumor visualized within the nasal vestibule floor and ala
Imaging showed thicker right ala compared to the left ala

salient_findings: Recurrent lesion of the right nasal vestibule mucosa

differentials: Primary mucinous carcinoma of the skin
per_call: Primary mucinous carcinoma of the skin

shortlist.label: Sweat gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent lesion with local invasion and histological features consistent with sweat gland origin

shortlist.label: Hidradenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Initial biopsy reported as solid and cystic hidradenoma with recurrence, suggesting malignant transformation

shortlist.label: Adnexal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion location and histological features consistent with adnexal origin

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the location and recurrence of the lesion

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, still a possibility given the location and local invasion

raw.rationale: The patient's initial biopsy was reported as a solid and cystic hidradenoma, which is a type of benign sweat gland tumor, but the recurrence and positive margins on the second excision, along with the clinical presentation, suggest a malignant transformation, making Hidradenocarcinoma the most likely diagnosis

rejected.label: Sweat gland carcinoma
rejected.why: Too broad, as hidradenocarcinoma is a specific type of sweat gland carcinoma

rejected.label: Adnexal carcinoma
rejected.why: Adnexal carcinoma is a broader term that encompasses various types of skin appendage tumors, but the specific diagnosis of hidradenocarcinoma is more precise

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The pathology results, including p63 positivity and the initial diagnosis of solid and cystic hidradenoma, do not support squamous cell carcinoma

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and pathology results do not align with basal cell carcinoma, which typically has distinct histological features
